extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, engineers, architects, educators and university/college administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and informal standards for (a) designing acoustically effective buildings and (b) organization and quality of technical/teacher education and related institutional arrangements, as discussed in a 1922 Nature issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher training standard (United States, 1922 bulletin)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard requirements as regards training for teaching in elementary and in high schools respectively are two years of normal-school work for the former and four years of college work with professional courses for the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted from Bulletin No. 2 of 1922 of the U.S. Bureau of Education summarizing responses by 520 superintendents; implies an evaluative baseline for teacher qualifications and hiring in elementary versus secondary schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary vs. high-school teacher pay/training recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The view that elementary school teachers should be as well trained and well paid as those of the high school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an argument promoted by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce pamphlet 'Know and Help your Schools'; noted that few school boards had adopted this view by 1922 — guidance for policy/evaluation rather than an established standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent practical and theoretical training in engineering education
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the student with all necessary practical training concurrently with his theoretical work, thus obviating the risk, incidental to sandwich systems, of forgetting in the works what was learned in the college and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim made by Loughborough Technical College (calendar 1922–23) as a quality criterion for engineering programs: integrate workshop/practical experience with classroom instruction rather than separating them into alternating blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sandwich-scheme apprenticeship duration (Merchant Venturers’ College)
rubrics_metrics.description: A special feature of the Bristol 'sandwich scheme' is that the student spends in the works 14 months between the first and second college (10-months) sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes an institutional standard for length and timing of workplace training within an academic-apprenticeship program; useful as a benchmark for evaluating apprenticeship structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship eligibility condition (Merchant Venturers’ College)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the free-tuition entrance scholarships is 'for the son of a citizen of Béthune who has passed either the B.-és-L. or B.-és-Sc. examination.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete eligibility criterion for a named scholarship; example of admission/award requirement based on citizenship and prior qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for mycologists and plant pathologists
rubrics_metrics.description: It is considered that mycologists and plant pathologists must be essentially botanists with the necessary fundamental training in chemistry and physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the British Mycological Society report: a stated professional-standard for training and disciplinary grounding required to carry out systematic mycology and plant pathology effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical grounding for plant pathologists (crop awareness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the plant pathologist a sense of crop values and of the important phases in the growth of crops should be inculcated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises that beyond laboratory/disciplinary training, plant pathologists need practical, applied understanding of crops to make diagnoses and recommendations relevant to agriculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for improved diagnostic clarity in pathogenic fungi
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention was directed to the inadequacy of the diagnosis of certain genera and species of pathogenic importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative criterion for taxonomic/diagnostic work: species- and genus-level diagnoses should be sufficiently clear and reliable where there is pathogenic significance; implies priority for systematic revision and improved diagnostic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary acoustic design objective: control of sound and reduction of noise
rubrics_metrics.description: With the present-day congestion of our towns... the reduction of noise becomes of constantly increasing importance... Need also exists for investigation on the most efficient means of propagating sound in order to secure its most effective transmission and reflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the editorial 'Acoustic Research': designers and evaluators should prioritize both suppression of unwanted noise and effective propagation (transmission/reflection) where sound is desired (e.g., auditoria). Calls for research into material and geometric controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditorium acoustics: many varying factors require case-specific design
rubrics_metrics.description: The production of an acoustically successful auditorium is frequently of paramount importance in connexion with architectural design... the variations in the factors which have to be considered are many, and no two designs are wholly identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance that there is no single formula; acoustic evaluation must consider multiple interacting factors unique to each hall — geometry, materials, intended use — and avoid one-size-fits-all prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider absorption as distinct design goal depending on room use
rubrics_metrics.description: The acoustic efficiency of public halls by any means the whole matter. There are more numerous cases in which the direct absorption of sound is of as great importance as is transmission in auditoria. In the hospital ward, the private sick-room, and in the office, where quiet and ventilation are so often incompatible, the best means of destroying unwanted sounds calls for scientific investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/evaluation criterion: for spaces where silence or reduced noise is the goal (wards, offices), prioritize absorption and sound-damping solutions, and balance these against other functional needs like ventilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to supply practical, simple scientific information to practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: If science is to have its due appreciation it must supply information of a practical and simple kind which will appeal to workers in a field already so wide that they have little time for the study of theory, however interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for researchers and communicators: present findings in accessible, practitioner-oriented formats so builders/architects can apply acoustic research without deep engagement with complex theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical laboratory research as a basis for acoustic design advice
rubrics_metrics.description: In the laboratory of acoustics built for Prof. Sabine... Prof. Sabine had collected a great deal of experimental data on sound in relation to materials, and his researches had sufficiently impressed themselves on American architects... The laboratory is now under the direction of Prof. Paul E. Sabine... work of this nature must eventually prove a valuable national asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for good practice: base acoustic design recommendations on controlled experimental measurements (materials, transmission, resonance) generated in dedicated acoustic laboratories; encourage consultation between experimentalists and architects.
